title: Eraser drag: one history entry PER POINTERMOVE (Flash 8 = one undo per gesture) + no-op increments still rewrite geometry
description:
VERIFIED by code inspection. Flash 8 treats an entire eraser gesture (pointerdown..pointerup) as ONE undoable edit. Ours pushes an undo entry per pointermove:
- StageArea.tsx:3170-3263 calls onShapeUpdate/onShapeDelete on EVERY move increment;
- Shell.tsx:1688-1695 handleShapeUpdate does pushDoc(...) (a history entry) per call.
A one-second scrub produces dozens of history entries; Ctrl+Z after erasing un-does a single 1-sample sliver. Contrast the shape-move path, which uses replaceDoc during the drag and a single pushDoc at gesture end (dragStartDocRef pattern, Shell.tsx:1747-1790).

SECONDARY: planarEraseShape (engine/planar/eraser.ts:121-210) ALWAYS reruns the read-back and returns a NEW Shape object even when nothing was erased (it early-returns the same reference only for empty stamp loops), and StageArea gates the update on 'next !== obj.shape' (:3237) which is therefore always true once the bbox pre-filter passes — so hovering-with-button-down over a shape without actually erasing anything still rewrites its geometry through the arrangement every move (doc churn, extra history entries, and repeated read-back round-trips that feed the task-1335 curve-degradation and task-1425 hole-refill defects).

SUGGESTED FIX: (1) during the eraser drag use replaceDoc (no history) for incremental updates and commit ONE pushDoc on pointerup from a pre-gesture snapshot — reuse the existing dragStartDocRef pattern; (2) make planarEraseShape return the ORIGINAL shape reference when erasedFace is empty and no stroke edge was dropped, so no-op increments are free and detectable.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e or store-level test — an eraser drag of N moves produces exactly ONE history entry; a single undo restores the pre-gesture artwork; a drag whose stamps never intersect the shape leaves the document reference unchanged. Related: 1425, 1335. Found by brush/eraser Flash-8 fidelity audit.
